question: A newborn girl is rushed to the neonatal ICU after an emergency cesarean section due to unstable vital signs after delivery. The pregnancy was complicated due to oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia. Gestation was at 38 weeks. APGAR scores were 6 and 8 at 1 and 5 minutes respectively. The newborn’s temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), the blood pressure is 60/40 mm Hg, the respiratory rate is 45/min, and the pulse is 140/min. Physical examination reveals irregularly contoured bilateral abdominal masses. Abdominal ultrasound reveals markedly enlarged echogenic kidneys (5 cm in the vertical dimension) with multiple cysts in the cortex and medulla. This patient is at highest risk of which of the following complications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia" -> "Compromised lung development" -> "Respiratory distress" -> "Hypoxia" -> "Systemic hypoperfusion" -> "Renal hypoperfusion" -> "Renal cysts and enlarged kidneys" -> "Renal failure" -> "Recurrent UTI" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Enlarged echogenic kidneys with multiple cysts" -> "Polycystic kidney disease" -> "Renal insufficiency" -> "Recurrent UTI" -> 70%
analysis: The newborn girl with markedly enlarged echogenic kidneys with multiple cysts likely has autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). This condition is associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis, which can lead to portal hypertension as a complication.
